CS5-01.note: The colon is an explicit gloss: 'a residue of manufacture with no bearing on how the sheet aged' = incidental. B and D are the two directions the evidence rules out; C is off-axis (deliberate vs accidental is a different contrast than consequential vs inconsequential). Clean but low-difficulty because the appositive does the work.

CS5-02.note: 'males recorded forty years apart shared the same terminal trill' fixes invariant. A and D both name variability (the state the larger archive actually finds), B names decay - none survives the 'since' clause. Difficulty sits in the vocabulary, not the reasoning.

CS5-03.note: Appositive gloss again: 'the slow agent of the material's ruin' = corrosive. C is the corrected view, not the blank. Same construction as CS5-01 and CS5-03 - two of the four completions in this batch are solved by an appositive rather than by the reversal.

CS5-04.second_defensible_note: C 'derivative' is dismissive too but does not follow from brevity, which is what the stem makes the sign; and the notes are demonstrably original (a disagreement carried over years).
CS5-04.note: Only the first sentence is load-bearing: brevity read as a sign of low engagement = perfunctory. The evidence sentence confirms but is not needed to choose. A is the contrary the evidence supports, so it is a real trap for students who read the reversal and fill the blank with the corrected view.

CS5-05.second_defensible_note: B 'Efficiency'. On the text as written, a theory that accommodates the same king lists and the same eclipse record with less machinery is describable as more efficient; 'theoretical efficiency' is idiomatic for exactly this. Parsimony is the more precise term for a count of unattested entities, but the passage does not contain anything that excludes B. Fix by replacing Efficiency, not by rewriting the key.
CS5-05.note: Best-built word-in-context item in the batch - all four are live senses of 'economy' and the passage's last sentence defines the intended one. It is also the one item where the second option genuinely survives.

CS5-06.second_defensible_note: A 'Enumerate' is the intended trap but is untenable: she does enumerate the losses (water height, the bridge, the sheep), so 'does not enumerate the loss' contradicts the passage.
CS5-06.note: Weak by the stated rule: C 'Withstand' and D 'Exaggerate' are not senses of 'register' at all and go without the passage. Real contest is a two-way A/B, which is why it still plays hard. Add two live senses (e.g. 'Record', 'Display') and it stops being half a four-option item.

CS5-07.note: 'settled in a way that satisfied nobody' plus an average nothing in the mechanics justified: the question was closed, not clarified. A is the sense a careless reader defaults to and the passage explicitly denies. C and D are not senses of 'settled', which costs the set some width.

CS5-08.second_defensible_note: A 'Unadorned'. The described operation is the removal of technical vocabulary, which is literally a stripping of ornament, and 'plainness is a choice rather than a limitation' reads naturally as a style claim. The text's justification is about the reader ('a report nobody outside the field can read is not a report'), which is why I pick C - but the sentence the word sits in supports A on its own.
CS5-08.note: The one item where I had to weigh a whole-text purpose against the local sentence to break the tie. That is a defensible SAT construction, but here the local sentence points the other way, which makes it a coin-flip for a strong student rather than a discrimination.

CS5-09.note: The last sentence names snow cover and nothing else; A, B and C name differences the text never mentions. Well-formed parallel frame, but there is no competition once the sentence is read.

CS5-10.second_defensible_note: B 'wages session musicians were paid elsewhere' is close but wrong: the passage compares the fee to 'a week's wage' generically, not to musicians' pay at other labels.
CS5-10.note: Weak on shape, not on content: D is the only option whose tail is a compound ('the fees it paid AND the masters it never issued') and the only one naming facts internal to the contracts rather than an outside comparator. Both tells are visible with the source covered. I do NOT read the key as field knowledge - see knowledge_key_agree.

CS5-11.passage_needed_reason: Answerable from restoration ecology alone. 'High seedling survival with no canopy gain because tended monoculture seedlings never close into stands' is the standard finding of the mangrove-planting literature; A, B and D are made-up confounds. I would have picked C with the passage covered.
CS5-11.difficulty_note: medium with the passage, trivial for anyone who knows the field
CS5-11.note: Option set is genuinely parallel and well built - the leak is the key's status as the field's received claim, not the option construction.

CS5-12.note: The next sentence names the guild rolls verbatim. A pure retrieval item.

CS5-13.note: The closing sentence adds biomass to clear against per-cut funding, i.e. workload. A is the trap for students who stop at 'raises flowering plant cover by about a quarter'. B is eliminable on register alone (the text urges nothing), which costs one option.

CS5-14.note: Two regions, eastern fits and western does not. A, B and C each mis-state one countable detail (centuries / coin weights / mints), so the item turns on a single word in each option.

CS5-15.note: 'only by a fifth of the gap' plus 'the remainder tracks the concentration of a small solute' is stated outright. Arithmetically decidable, so no ambiguity - and no difficulty.

CS5-16.note: The final clause ('whose awkward inversions fall exactly at the points the Hebrew marks') states the benefit. But A, B and C all assign the inversions a deficit and D alone a benefit, and the text is shaped as a rehabilitation - see act_mismatch_agree.

CS5-17.passage_needed_reason: Fixed park stations versus volunteer mobile transects is the canonical urban-heat-island study design; D names it and A, B and C name comparators that no such study makes. I would have picked D with the source covered.
CS5-17.note: Parallel frame is correct and the passage does state D, but the key is recoverable as the standard method of the field.

CS5-18.note: B is explicitly refuted in the text ('The province was not isolated'), C and D are never claimed. Retrieval.

CS5-19.passage_needed_reason: 'Actigraphy reads stillness as sleep' is the textbook limitation of actigraphy and B is that limitation stated. Given only Text 1's finding and the four options, I would pick B on method knowledge. Not on the blind solvers' flag list but it belongs to the same family as 11 and 17.
CS5-19.note: Text 2 does state B in its last sentence, so the key is right; the exposure is that the key is the field's stock objection.

CS5-20.passage_needed_reason: Standard agronomy: a rotation gain over continuous cereal at matched fertiliser is attributed to legume nitrogen. C is additionally false of any rotation (a rotation lengthens, not shortens, the interval between cereal crops) and is eliminable on subject knowledge alone; D is off-topic. Another unflagged member of the knowledge family.
CS5-20.note: Correct and clean on the text, but neither the passage nor much of the option set is doing work.

CS5-21.note: Text 2's first clause is the counting-method change; the household-survey sentence blocks C by making surveys Text 2's own evidence. B and D are unsupported. Solid, if easy.

CS5-22.second_defensible_note: C is the trap: Text 2 asserts the higher desk-reject rate, but Text 1 says nothing about it, so there is no agreement to point at. Agreement items require both authors, and only A clears that bar.
CS5-22.note: Good use of the agreement stem - Text 2 disputes only the cause, conceding the count. The discrimination is real.

CS5-23.second_defensible_note: D 'explains neither gap once time on task has been matched' is the near miss and is refuted by the semicolon clause: with time matched, recall equalises but reproduction does not, so motor rehearsal still explains the reproduction gap. A inverts the logic - if the recall gap only appears when time differs, time is the explanation, not rehearsal.
CS5-23.note: Hardest and best item in the batch. The choice turns on one clause after a semicolon that a fast reader drops, and every option is a live position until that clause is read.

CS5-24.second_defensible_note: D names snowpack; Text 2 names the water table and the wet winters that refilled the aquifer. Adjacent, but C is what the text measures.
CS5-24.passage_needed_reason: The Yellowstone trophic-cascade revision - willow height tracking the water table rather than wolf-driven browsing pressure - is the standard published rebuttal, and C is that rebuttal. Given Text 1 and the option set alone I would pick C. Not on the blind flag list; same family as 11, 17, 19, 20.
CS5-24.note: Well-built parallel options; the leak is the key's status as the received counter-claim.

items.CS5-04: partial. Two options, D perfunctory and C derivative, are dismissive readings of an annotator's engagement, so the stem's axis narrows the field to two rather than to one. A blind solver has a coin flip, not a gift. The bigger issue is a different one: only the first sentence is needed even with the source in hand.
items.CS5-06: agree, and worse than described. C Withstand and D Exaggerate are not senses of 'register' in any register of English, so they go on word knowledge before the axis argument is even reached. The item is effectively two options wide.
items.CS5-08: agree. A, B and D all characterise the prose itself (unadorned / forthright / unfinished); C alone characterises the reader's relation to it, and the stem's surrounding text is entirely about the reader. Compounding it, this is also the item where I judged a second option defensible, so the axis tell and the ambiguity point in opposite directions - a blind solver lands on C and a careful reader can defend A.
items.CS5-16: agree. A, B and C each attribute a deficit to the inversions and D alone a benefit, against a text whose shape is a rehabilitation. Fixable without touching the key: make at least two distractors state benefits the text does not support (e.g. that the inversions preserve the Hebrew's sound, or that they help readers locate quotations).

act_mismatch_agree.summary: Three of the four hold from the with-source seat; item 4 narrows to two options rather than one. Note that 6 and 8 are also the two items I rated hard, so the act tell is concentrated in exactly the items the batch is relying on for its ceiling.

items.CS5-10: disagree as stated. The key is a recap of the passage's own two facts, not a claim the field holds; 1920s flat-fee contracts have no standard revisionist verdict a solver could import. But the item IS blind-solvable for a different reason, which I would rather see recorded accurately: D is the only compound option and the only one naming facts internal to the arrangement while A, B and C all reach for an outside comparator. That is a shape tell, and a fix aimed at 'knowledge' would miss it.
items.CS5-11: agree. High seedling survival with flat canopy area because tended plantings never close into stands is the received finding of the mangrove-restoration literature.
items.CS5-17: agree. Fixed park stations versus volunteer mobile transects is the canonical urban-heat-island design; the key names the method, not a result.
items.CS5-23: disagree. The field's stock claim would be 'handwriting helps because of motor rehearsal', which is Text 1's position, not the key. The key requires the clause after the semicolon separating recall from reproduction, and D - the answer a solver reaches by generalising 'the effect goes away when you control time' - is wrong precisely because of that clause. This is the one item in the batch where the source is doing all the work.

unflagged_members.CS5-19: actigraphy reads stillness as sleep - the textbook limitation, stated as the key.
unflagged_members.CS5-20: rotation gain at matched fertiliser attributed to legume nitrogen - standard agronomy; distractor C is additionally false of any rotation.
unflagged_members.CS5-24: willow height tracking the water table rather than wolf-driven browsing - the standard published rebuttal to the Yellowstone cascade account.

knowledge_key_agree.summary: Two of four flagged items confirmed, two refused - and three unflagged items belong to the same family. The family is larger than the blind pass caught and it clusters in the paired-text block (19, 20, 24 are consecutive paired-text items). The common shape is a paired-text stem whose Text 2 states the discipline's known objection to Text 1: the option set can be perfectly parallel and the item still answers itself.
